verdict.rationale: mParticle ships a documented Warehouse Sync feature (Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery, Databricks) with a Warehouse Sync API and SQL reference, letting engineers pull warehouse tables into mParticle for audience/profile use [mparticle-docs-x4][mparticle-docs-18]. However this is ingestion, not warehouse-native activation — the docs explicitly describe it as syncing/copying data into mParticle rather than defining models and activating audiences directly on tables in place without re-collection, which is the core of the reverse-ETL/warehouse-native story. Missing for 10: evidence of querying/modeling directly on warehouse tables without copying data into mParticle, and activation flows that bypass ingestion entirely.
